rv.q: In the end, this bold, darkly funny, and unexpectedly tender work stands as a testament to the theater’s capacity to anatomize intimacy without anesthetizing it: a funny, poignant hour that leaves its audience pondering not only these two characters but the mysterious machinery of desire itself.

Now if all of that intellectual psychological explanation, exploration, and questioning has sparked your interest in HardLove, and piqued your curiosity about finding out more about yourself, then I suggest you’ll enjoy the play.

HardLove both captures the particular frisson of that period where two people are feeling each other out–and up–for the first time and uses it to open out onto broader examinations of identity and relationship, all in one fantastic, funny hour.

cn.t: Critics find this intimate two-hander a compelling exploration of desire and connection that invites personal interpretation. Strong chemistry and nuanced writing earn praise in this thought-provoking production.
